video.description:
Learn to explain how to configure where SwiftData stores data and keep values unique: ModelConfiguration, In-Memory Store & Unique Constraint, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
ModelConfiguration - An object that describes how SwiftData stores your models, such as whether it uses the disk.
In-Memory Store - A store that keeps data only in memory, so it disappears when the app quits.
Unique Constraint - A rule that allows only one stored item with a given value, such as one account per email.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain ModelConfiguration, In-Memory Store and Unique Constraint in English?

dialogue.title: Tests that leave no trace
dialogue.setting: Writing tests for the user store

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my tests leave old users on the disk.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use an in-memory store for tests. The data disappears when the test ends.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do I turn that on?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With a ModelConfiguration, like `mem` in our code. Set `isStoredInMemoryOnly` to true.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the ModelConfiguration decides where the data lives?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, that is its job. It also holds other storage settings.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now a test fails. Two users have the same `id`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add a unique constraint. In our code, `@Attribute(.unique)` does that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So SwiftData keeps only one user for each `id`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. The unique constraint stops duplicates.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Great. Tests use the in-memory store, and the model has a unique constraint.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And pass the ModelConfiguration to the container.
Pass a ModelConfiguration to the container.
